# Reference fixtures

The GPU/GTE fixtures are derived from Jakub Czekański's
[ps1-tests](https://github.com/JaCzekanski/ps1-tests/tree/f727802fead11f1daa7549285548392ef87749cb),
commit `f727802fead11f1daa7549285548392ef87749cb`. Its MIT licence is retained
in `ps1-tests-LICENSE.txt`. No expected values are generated by this renderer.

## GPU captures

`gpu_reference.h` contains FNV-1a 64-bit hashes of RGB555 words, low byte first.
The input is each published `gpu/<case>/vram.png`, with R/G/B reduced by `>>3`.
PNGs cannot establish bit 15; mask/STP behavior has separate arithmetic tests.
The replayed packet cases in `../test_raster_reference.c` follow the upstream
test sources. These are reference image comparisons; we did not capture new
hardware output, and upstream does not label every PNG with its capture unit.

| Case | Compared region | Input PNG SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| triangle | All 1024x512 pixels, hashed per row | `d5a03568f66ee69efed3cc8516d7b79d32a2733e879ba6c543d55612ee9c9144` |
| uv-interpolation | All 1024x512 pixels, widths 0..255 | `363c37b1f37555a8f1f0f0810dcaf05c59a0ff7cc6d67afb2da6345221b75113` |
| lines | (0,0) 320x100 and (0,100) 148x132, hashed per row | `2e04988670abba6d0d4d8693b9df55b12c6e8a945f52b9db2b727b6411d8cf5b` |
| vram-to-vram-overlap | 147 rectangles, each 40x26, excluding labels/grid | `28cd11886418438e76fafd970f990205ffe6fd776e755b846ab427fa86c305af` |
| clut-cache | (0,0) 1024x256, hashed per row; all 13 cases | `c59292e35df4eae6dbc80fa44991ad2d5ff4a432535e65fce3b3681889c56d9c` |

This checks 1,515,136 RGB555 pixels. The omitted line regions use an
uninitialized polyline colour or the upstream SDK's trigonometry; they are not
silently accepted. Triangle origin/tie order, small gradients, shallow/steep
lines and transfer overlap are covered, but these examples are not an exhaustive
GPU packet corpus.

`../test_texture_cache.c` replays `gpu/clut-cache/main.c`, including the three
texture uploads, drawing over the palette, explicit cache clears, mode changes
and horizontal CLUT wrap. All 256 rows match the published PNG. An optional
second argument `uncached` produces the old immediate-read behavior for visual
comparison; five rows disagree. The fixture shows 8-bit-to-4-bit CLUT reuse
(row 152), unlike Mednafen's depth-equality cache tag. We follow the captured
result and retain the full palette. A 4-bit-to-8-bit draw reloads it.
Separate focused tests cover texture-line eviction, transfer invalidation,
clipped CLUT loads, page/window changes, GPU reset and the water clear+move.
These establish command ordering, not GPU bus contention or scanout timing.

## GTE captures

`gte_reference.h` extracts 368 of the 1,150 vectors in `gte/test-all/tests.c`.
The upstream [hardware log](https://github.com/JaCzekanski/ps1-tests/blob/f727802fead11f1daa7549285548392ef87749cb/gte/test-all/psx.log)
reports all 1,150 passing on PSX. The source file SHA-256 is
`10136d1335069b8f8e4d5e3f1c1f197a7c4ec1e7606ece1aa658a8c0d1706240`.

The selection matches the port's existing opcode API: RTPS/RTPT with sf=1,
lm=0; all MVMVA selector/sf/lm combinations present upstream; NCLIP, SQR,
AVSZ3/AVSZ4; and NCS/NCT/NCCS/NCCT/NCDS/NCDT/CC/CDP with sf=1, lm=1.
The harness models register write order (including SXYP and IRGB side effects),
then compares data registers 7..31 and FLAG. Other opcode variants are not
claimed as covered. Original test IDs are retained for diagnosis.

## Reproduction

Keep an upstream checkout outside tracked game sources, then run:

```powershell
python tests/fixtures/generate_references.py --source E:/_SOURCE/_CODE/ps1-tests --check
```

The generator requires Python and Pillow, verifies input digests, and compares
the generated text with the checked-in fixtures. Omit `--check` to regenerate.
It does not download source or read the renderer's output.

## PAL damage routines

`combat_armour_reference.h` contains 130 numeric cases produced by executing
the original armour helpers at `0x80057A9C` and `0x80057BE4`.
`combat_camera_reference.h` contains 132 cases for outer damage `0x80057D54`,
the established `PlayerThink` feedback block `0x8003AE10..0x8003AFA8`, and
view-offset composition `0x80038260`. The latter's only retail caller applies
the result to the weapon. Cases include zero and nonzero initial amplitudes,
all 22 mod values, signed/zero damage, left/right impacts, armour and skill.

The generator uses a bounded R3000 integer interpreter with branch/load delays
and little-endian unaligned accesses. Isolated armour cases record the fade
call; player cases execute the real fade and impact-shock routines and hook
only memset, axis-vector normalisation and burn/pain sample dispatch. The
PlayerThink block receives its established client/entity register bindings.
This is numeric machine-code evidence, not a full hardware playthrough.

Both generated files identify the exact PAL SLES-01534 loaded-segment SHA-256.
The generator verifies that hash before execution. Extract the segment from
the user's disc and keep it outside tracked source:

```powershell
.\build-msvc\bin\Release\q2psx-inspect.exe exe .install/disc/game.cue .agents/tmp/functional-parity/damage-audit/pal-executable.bin
python tests/fixtures/generate_combat_reference.py .agents/tmp/functional-parity/damage-audit/pal-executable.bin --output tests/fixtures/combat_armour_reference.h --camera-output tests/fixtures/combat_camera_reference.h
```

The headers contain numeric inputs/results only; they do not redistribute
retail instructions. `test_combat` and `test_sim` consume the checked-in values
without requiring the disc or the generator.

## SPU capture fixtures

For final CD/main register programming, see the separate PAL fixture below;
the pre-volume waveform captures in this section do not measure those gains.

`spu_reference.h` retains PCM samples and synthetic ADPCM stimuli from the
PCSX-Redux authors' [Nugget hardware tests](https://github.com/pcsx-redux/nugget/tree/4dc70d2931121a0fde858a0354192b6df4fa22e8/tests/spu),
commit `4dc70d2931121a0fde858a0354192b6df4fa22e8`. Their MIT notice is retained
in `spu_reference_LICENSE.txt`. `spu_reference_sources.json` pins the Git blob
hashes of the source stimuli and published `.test.pcm` captures. These are
upstream hardware measurements, not new captures made in this project.

The 28 selected cases cover all five valid ADPCM predictors, cross-block state,
positive/negative saturation, shifts 0–11, selected invalid filter codes,
loop-start/repeat behavior, silence/sine/square/triangle waves and pitches
`0800`, `1000`, `1300`, `1400`, `1500`, `2000` and `3000`. The `1300` case
uses a seven-sample sine to exercise sixteen fractional filter positions.
`test_spu.c` checks exact amplitudes and repeats each reference for 768 samples.

The signal is voice 1's pre-volume SPU capture RAM at 44,100 Hz. Upstream's
`000f/1fc0` ADSR settles at `ENVX=3fff`; voice/main volume does not scale this
capture. The generator removes only the declared warmup, with one exception:
predictor 3 has an unperiodized prefix that depends on prior predictor state,
so the unchanged final 224 samples (two complete loops) are retained. No
amplitudes are adjusted or regenerated.

The harness searches capture-ring rotation. Pitches `1500` and `2000` also
need seven and two initial source-phase classes, respectively: their stride
and 28-sample waveform period share a factor, as upstream's `spu-capture.c`
explains. All other cases use one class. This alignment cannot establish
absolute key-on phase, bus latency or history across a hardware key-on.

Three published captures are explicitly excluded: `adpcm_edge_shift_12_15`
does not yet match the reserved-shift fallback; `adpcm_edge_flag_end_mute`
and `adpcm_edge_flag_end_repeat` include finite startup/transition behavior
outside this repeating-period comparison. Dedicated local boundary tests
check END/repeat, but are not substitutes for those two waveform captures.
General ADSR settings, remaining fractional filter positions, final mixed
volume, XA decoding and host output conversion are not established by this corpus.

To reproduce from the pinned upstream source directory:

```powershell
python tests/fixtures/generate_spu_reference.py --source E:/_SOURCE/_CODE/nugget --check
```

The generator requires only Python, checks every consumed source/capture hash,
and does not download files or read local decoder output. Omit `--check` to
regenerate the header. The existing SPU coefficient table has separate GPLv2-or-later
attribution in `src/audio/spu_gauss.h` and the repository README.

## PAL CD and main-volume registers

`audio_register_reference.h` records the actual MMIO writes made by the PAL
main-volume setup at `0x8007248c..0x800724a8`, CD-input setup at
`0x80071adc..0x80071b0c`, and all 512 stereo/volume combinations of
`SetCDVolume` at `0x80071b9c`. The bounded R3000 interpreter executes the SDK
routines as well, with branch/load delays and indexed CD-register writes.
It verifies that the CD matrix is latched, and records the main direct-volume
words `3fc0/3fc0` and CD-input words `7fff/7fff`. No SDK call is substituted.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_audio_reference.py .agents/tmp/functional-parity/damage-audit/pal-executable.bin --check
```

The generator checks the PAL loaded-segment SHA-256 before execution and emits
numeric results only. `test_sound_pitch` combines the native matrix rows with
signed fixed-point test vectors; `test_client_audio` checks the production mix
order and gains. These establish register programming and software arithmetic,
not independent hardware measurements of final amplitude, clipping or latency.

## CD-XA interpolation software reference

`xa_resample_reference.h` contains little-endian PCM hashes from compiling the
Mednafen/Beetle PSX CD-controller interpolation functions unchanged, with a
small input driver. The pinned source is
[`cdc.c` at de6e32cf78f4403766167bfbe83f33074efeb83e](https://github.com/libretro/beetle-psx-libretro/blob/de6e32cf78f4403766167bfbe83f33074efeb83e/mednafen/psx/cdc.c),
Git blob `0ed59c322adababa0a2ac6165cd1c9b3aaeafc6f`, licensed GPLv2 or later
(compatible with this repository's GPLv2). The extracted reference retains
that source's license notice. The production coefficient table has matching
attribution in `src/audio/xa_impulse.h` and the repository README.

Six signals exercise independent left/right impulses, signed DC, extrema,
alternating samples, deterministic noise, and saturating step transitions.
Each runs through three consecutive sectors without resetting history.
The 18 hashes cover all 84,672 interleaved output samples, including startup,
every phase, ring-buffer wrap and sector boundaries. Each 2,016-frame source
sector produces exactly 2,352 output frames. The separate client tests check
native SPU-clock consumption, live gain, release tails, stream resets and
movie clock/fade conversion at 44,100 Hz.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_xa_reference.py --source <pinned-cdc.c> --work-dir .agents/tmp/xa-reference --check
```

The generator verifies the entire source's Git blob hash, then builds only
the upstream coefficient table, buffer reader, volume matrix and resampler
plus the fixture driver. It neither links nor reads the port's resampler.
Omit `--check` to regenerate the numeric header. The temporary CMake build
belongs under the project's temporary area and is disposable after checking.

This is a software differential test, not a hardware capture. Published CD-XA
filter descriptions leave small rounding differences unresolved; the fixture
does not establish those bits, the XA predictor, or the absolute CD-start phase.

## PAL resource allocation

`world_resource_reference.h` contains 30 numeric forced-packet cases generated
by executing both native resource loaders (`0x80070EA4`, `0x80071498`) and
packet initialization (`0x80070AA8`, stopping before its allocation call).
Each case repeats with four explicitly injected largest-block values. The
signed override, round-up and mesh default/disable cases must agree across
all eight executions. `test_subdiv_pool` uses these results; no expected
capacity is calculated from the port's allocator.

The same generator executes native heap initialization, first-fit/last-fit
allocation, Free and the largest-block probe without substituting those
functions. It confirms 1,117,872 initial payload bytes and distinguishes the
largest fragmented hole from total free space. Another 180 native loader runs
record automatic-policy behavior for selected heap inputs and positive
controls, including subtraction underflow and allocation/default boundaries.
Eighteen automatic boundary rows are now also stored in the header and checked
against `q2_world_subdiv_resources_heap` for all five nonnegative controls. This
qualifies the policy given a heap value; it does not qualify the client's heap
history. The separate loader trace below supplies real allocation histories for
selected scenarios.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_resource_reference.py .agents/tmp/functional-parity/damage-audit/pal-executable.bin tests/fixtures/world_resource_reference.h --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/flat-packets/native-resource-reference.json --check
```

The generator verifies the PAL segment SHA-256 and emits numeric results only.
Its shared bounded R3000 runner models branch/load delays and rejects
unsupported instructions. No retail code is stored in the fixture.

## PAL and US loader heap traces

`generate_heap_reference.py` reads the user's disc without extracting assets,
loads a verified PAL or US executable segment into isolated RAM, and executes the
native file loader, archive relocation, creature-module initialization, image
decoder, session pools and resource allocation policy. CD reads and BIOS
strings/copies use explicit host hooks. GPU transfers, critical sections/cache
operations and SPU sample upload are stubbed. BIOS `rand` uses an explicit seed
of one and the documented [BIOS generator](https://psx-spx.consoledev.net/ps1/kernelbios/misc-functions/#a2fh-rand).
These are allocation traces, not hardware timing or whole-machine captures.

The default segment is PAL SLES-01534. `--ntsc` selects US SLUS-00757 and
verifies segment SHA-256
`8f61c897173a4109532191c4f25a00bd198d6f3a4d4d6bdcfd9e1204f768a214`.
The segment is the executable payload after its 2,048-byte PS-X EXE header,
limited to the header's declared payload size. US entry points, globals, BSS
and GP use the repository's verified address layout, checked against the US
symbol table; the interpreter executes the US instructions themselves.
The heap begins at `0x800EE718` on PAL and `0x800EE988` on US. The physical
ceiling remains `0x801FF600` for both.

The representative suite covers BASE1 (including zone 1 and a return to zone 0),
JAIL2, POWER1, LAB, BOSS1, QFRONT, QFMV, MATRIX6 with two/three/four views, and
four-player TIMS, whose US packet budget crosses a block boundary after the fix.
Mission selection now executes `GameNewMission` and its direct-level lookup,
which reads the signed id at level-table `+0x16`. Multiplayer executes
`GameReRunMPLevel` first, selecting the null initializer (id 7, no allocation).
The earlier fixtures incorrectly selected id 6, the separate Tribute mission,
for multiplayer. Those were valid allocation traces for an artificial input,
not evidence for retail multiplayer startup. The regenerated fixtures remove
that four-byte record and its 28-byte header.
`--reload` additionally executes the native full-map unload and reload in each
case. The loading-screen image-list reset at `0x8006E25C` is supplied before
reload, matching the outer caller's precondition. The full unload leaves water
and mission allocations live; the next loader releases water later.

`heap_reference.h` contains only numeric operation arguments, native return
values, allocation counts and FNV-1a hashes of every ordered address/size pair.
`test_nativeheap` replays those operations through the port's accounting model
and compares after each operation, including failed probes, zero-byte allocations,
tail shrink, prefix release and fragmented placement. It does not derive
expected heap states from the C implementation. JSON retains readable snapshots,
phase capacities, explicit hooks and errors. Failed runs cannot emit fixtures.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_heap_reference.py .agents/tmp/functional-parity/damage-audit/pal-executable.bin .install/disc/game.cue --suite --reload --output .agents/tmp/functional-parity/mission-selection/pal-load.json --header tests/fixtures/heap_reference.h --budget-header tests/fixtures/level_memory_reference.h --check
```

`level_memory_reference.h` adds archive lengths/prefixes, media header and
palette sizes, session settings and final native heap states for 24 PAL load
phases. `level_memory_ntsc_reference.h` records the same 24 phases on US.
The expected capacities and address/size hashes come from the native
execution above; file metadata comes directly from the disc. `test_nativeheap`
also replays these phases through `levelmemory.c`. No port-generated expected
result is used.

`--session` retains native RAM through 17 full loads: QFRONT, BASE1, BASE2,
QENDMIS1, JAIL2, QENDMIS2, POWER1, QENDMIS3, LAB, QENDMIS4, BOSS1, QENDMIS5,
QFMV, QFRONT, two-player MATRIX6, four-player MATRIX6 and QFRONT. It executes
the native full unload, mission dispatcher and loader in their outer caller's
order. Campaign entry ids come from the native level-table lookup; the fixture
explicitly carries the departing id through intermission/movie screens and
selects the view count. It does not execute the entire campaign state machine
or prove every route's choice of those settings. `level_memory_session_reference.h`
and `level_memory_ntsc_session_reference.h` hold these 34 phases, bringing
the total to 82.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_heap_reference.py '<US-segment>' '<US-disc.cue>' --ntsc --suite --reload --output .agents/tmp/functional-parity/mission-selection/ntsc-load.json --budget-header tests/fixtures/level_memory_ntsc_reference.h --check
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_heap_reference.py '<PAL-segment>' '<PAL-disc.cue>' --session --output .agents/tmp/functional-parity/mission-selection/pal-session.json --budget-header tests/fixtures/level_memory_session_reference.h --check
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_heap_reference.py '<US-segment>' '<US-disc.cue>' --ntsc --session --output .agents/tmp/functional-parity/mission-selection/ntsc-session.json --budget-header tests/fixtures/level_memory_ntsc_session_reference.h --check
```

The client now supplies its loaded archives and session settings to this
accounting model. `test_client_memory --headless <disc.cue>` runs the same phases
through the real client, checking actual renderer capacities and every ordered
heap address/size hash. Its regular CTest invocation checks the unknown-layout
fallback without requiring a disc. With a disc, it chooses that revision's
fixtures and checks both the 24-load suite and 17-load session sequence.
All 82 model phases pass 4,649 checks including primitive operations; the
disc-backed client passes 520 checks on each revision. The
resource census also loads all 115 zones on each disc without accounting
fallback (1,418 checks per disc).
This broader load coverage is not a native reference comparison for every
zone. Arbitrary mission/session selection, recording allocations, other disc
revisions and hardware timing remain outside these fixtures.

`generate_mission_reference.py` independently executes all 51 named direct-level
selections on each revision and 11 successive selector calls per revision,
including default new game, each campaign unit, Tribute and null mission. The
resulting `level_mission_reference.h` checks the client's table reader, including
the real empty-name sentinel and the PAL/US COLOSSEUM/COLISEUM spelling. The
four-byte Tribute allocation is not a multiplayer allocation. Its two level
names have no shipped directories.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_mission_reference.py '<PAL-segment>' '<US-segment>' tests/fixtures/level_mission_reference.h --output .agents/tmp/functional-parity/mission-selection/mission-reference.json --check
```

## Native music selection and termination

`generate_music_reference.py` reads the two original CUEs and verifies the
same PAL/US executable hashes as the loader fixtures. It executes `GetToc`,
including the SDK TOC builder, and then `PlayTrackList`, `CdCheckMusic`,
`SeekAndPlay` and `PlayThisXA`. CD commands/device replies, file lookup and
callback registration are explicit hooks. The JSON records those boundaries;
this is not drive timing or waveform evidence.

`music_playlist_reference.h` contains only numeric selector/timer results and
directory keys. All 51 named rows per revision are covered, including stub
directories and immediately stopped lists. Fifteen selections per nonempty
list cover at least two complete cycles, for 1,170 starts across both builds.
All select XA ids 2..21. Separate calls cover all 22 selectors per revision and
four `PlayThisXA` no-op inputs per revision. GetToc leaves the static music
table unchanged; reserved ids 0/1 still have zero duration.

Four deliberately supplied RAM playlists per revision test empty lists,
one-/two-track finite lists and an explicit negative loop. They are labeled
synthetic inputs, not shipped playlists. Native zero termination stops; the
client previously restarted finite lists and failed both controls per disc.
`test_client_audio --music <disc.cue>` checks the client against all these
results (3,156 checks per disc). Its ordinary disc-backed run includes them.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_music_reference.py .install/disc/game.cue '<US-disc.cue>' --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/cdda/native-music.json --check
```

## Native actor ambient initialization and recovery

`generate_actor_light_reference.py` verifies the same PAL/US executable hashes
as the loader fixtures. It executes the original entity allocator, 25 player
spawn prefixes per revision (single player and all six mode selectors, four
owners each), and the complete ambient fade for every byte value at targets
32 and 64. The two revisions agree on all 1,024 fade calls. The player cases
stop immediately after both colour stores, before later placement.

It also reads all 166 creature-module occurrences on each disc and executes
each distinct relocated image's export 2, followed by the native shared spawn
wrapper and export 0. All 24 PAL and 25 US images retain the allocator's RGB
64 without writing current/target ambient. The native link and walk/fly/swim
start routines execute. Explicit hooks supply a separate AI edict, successful
neutral geometry/model records, sound services, class-method registration and
shadow registration; neutral cvar records are supplied. Unsupported imports
trap. The JSON records module hashes, source paths, colour writes and hooks.
These fixtures do not establish every spawn flag/difficulty combination or
whole-machine behavior, and no original instructions/assets are exported.

`actor_light_reference.h` contains only numeric colours and fade results.
`test_sim` checks first spawn, all four player slots, refresh, respawn and
32 recovery ticks against them. `test_client_creatures --headless-ambient`
uses the actual creature/player-body renderer and writes engine framebuffers.
The regular `--headless` creature suite also includes those cases.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_actor_light_reference.py .install/disc/game.cue '<US-disc.cue>' --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/actor-ambient/native.json --check
```

## Native player-body animation

`generate_player_animation_reference.py` verifies the same PAL/US executable
hashes as the loader fixtures and executes complete `player_anim`, advance and
install routines. The 4,080 calls per revision cover every current/request
pair, boundaries, jump contact flags, varying deltas, RNG state and twelve
120-step histories. Only BIOS randomness is hooked in these animation calls.
The ten input ranges are deliberately synthetic; emitted values are numeric
state, not original code or assets. Both revisions agree.

It also executes the loader's full scaling function on a synthetic model,
then the player-binding prefix through the two Stand/Run rest stores. These
confirm block D's start/end/rest conversion by five and the two loop rewinds.
Forty-eight joined bounded selector cases per revision supply explicit jump
and weapon return values; intervening player physics and weapon code are not
executed. This fixture does not prove full-frame order or that the client's
shot-counter proxy equals the native weapon return. Dry-fire and substep
return handling remain in the functional audit.

`test_playerdeath` checks every native animation state and RNG result.
`test_client_split` exercises four owners, damage consumption, non-ticking
updates and offscreen death/respawn. `test_client_creatures
--headless-player-animation <disc> <output>` uses the actual Male2 model and
engine framebuffer, including repeated pose sampling at four display deltas.
The regular `--headless` creature suite includes this fixture too.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_player_animation_reference.py .install/disc/game.cue '<US-disc.cue>' --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/player-animation/native.json --check
```

## Native grenade toss and rebound

`generate_toss_reference.py` verifies the PAL/US executable hashes and executes
2,592 complete `0x80046B98` toss calls per revision. The shared mover and SDK
square-root/normalization instructions execute with explicit entity/hull
collision outputs. Cases vary timestep, gravity, velocities, attitudes,
contact normals, clipped fractions, rest/held flags and shared RNG state.
The 192 entries of each SDK table also match their integer reconstruction.

Only collision services, rotation-matrix output and BIOS services are hooked.
GTE SQR/GPF and register transfers are modeled, so these are independent native
CPU fixtures, not hardware GTE captures. No code, assets or tables from the
executable are exported; `toss_reference.h` contains numeric input/output.

`test_weapon` compares integration, rebound, flags, attitude and RNG with
these results. `test_sim` checks real routing through runtime geometry,
three-point glass damage, actor priority and expiry ordering. The opt-in
`test_client_weapon --headless-grenade <disc> <output>` uses real MATRIX5
geometry for engine captures and BASE1 for cold-save continuation of moving
and resting grenades. It also checks bounce-sample lookup and queue draining.
Owner-mask lifetime, full actor-query equivalence and hardware sound order
remain outside this fixture's claim.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_toss_reference.py .install/disc/game.cue '<US-disc.cue>' --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/grenade-bounce/native.json --check
```

## Native projectile owner gates and actor contacts

`generate_projectile_contact_reference.py` verifies the same PAL/US executable
hashes and executes 768 bounded Grenade2/Grenade3 owner-gate prefixes plus 3,072
complete `0x800544EC` actor queries per revision. The owner cases initialize
registers and bounds explicitly; they stop before movement. Query cases execute
the native root, quadratic, fractional division and box helpers without hooks.
GTE operations use the toss fixture's model; no hardware-capture claim is made.
Five named integration probes additionally record the exact contacts used by
the simulation tests. A missing launcher `s3` initialization was corrected
from its prologue before accepting the owner-helper comparisons.

The two revisions agree on the emitted numeric input/output. `test_combat`
compares the replacement query's selected actor and exact clipped point with
all 3,072 cases. The previous query differs in 860 cases. `test_weapon` checks
all 768 owner-gate results and sequential leave/return behavior. All five live
projectile kinds now use the query; `test_sim` checks immune blockers, clipped
points, owner filtering, all player/creature owners and single-player fuses.
Hitscan/AI callers retain their older paths and need separate qualification.

`test_client_weapon --headless-projectile-contact <disc> <output>` captures a
real BASE1 owner contact and compares eight uninterrupted/cold-loaded ticks.
The save holds one cleared mask back inside the expanded box and another
still-armed mask. It also checks collision-cell continuation: projectile cell
restoration must use PrimaryColl, not the player's SecondaryColl. These are
focused contact/save tests, not a full-machine or whole-frame equivalence claim.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_projectile_contact_reference.py .install/disc/game.cue '<US-disc.cue>' --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/projectile-contact/native.json --check
```

## Native bolt sweep and effect sequence

`generate_bolt_reference.py` executes the complete PAL/US `0x80047C6C` sweep,
including the actor query and blood-spawn instructions. The executable hashes
are verified. All 192 cases agree between revisions: lifetime boundaries,
actor/type-2 entity/hull contacts, flight, individual flag gates and signed
halfword movement with negative and overflowing deltas. The header contains
numeric results; the local JSON records each service sequence and hook.

Entity/hull collision results, damage, sound, view setup and effect allocation
are explicit services. View count is zero, so body packet submission is outside
the claim. Particle vectors/offsets are recorded at allocation; hashes cover
all arguments, and the returned scratch record captures blood acceleration.
The fixture does not qualify the native cached hull marcher, posed-model hit
refinement, real audio or hardware GPU output.

`test_sim` compares final position/liveness, damage routing, light placement,
effect anchors, counts, ramps, motion and the full sweep's RNG result. It seeds
and checks the saved combat stream, which now serves both bolt trail and impact
draws. Broader cross-subsystem RNG sharing remains open. The opt-in
`test_client_weapon --headless-bolt <disc> <output>` uses BASE1 for a real
framebuffer capture and 32-step cold-save continuation through impact.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_bolt_reference.py .install/disc/game.cue '<US-disc.cue>' --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/bolt-sequence/native.json --check
```

## Native player auto-aim

`generate_autoaim_reference.py` verifies the PAL/US executable hashes and runs
the complete `0x80039DDC` search, RotMatrix, actor query, ratan2 and VectorNormal.
All 256 numeric cases per revision agree. Synthetic actors cover every ray,
nonzero pitch/yaw/roll, four window indices, failed projected-screen filters,
occlusion, owner exclusion and a null window. PrimaryColl results are supplied
per ray. The GTE model is the existing toss fixture, and actors have no posed
refinement; this is not hardware or whole-frame acceptance data.

`test_combat` checks selected actors, directions, pitch and exact visibility
segments. `test_client_weapon --headless-autoaim <disc> <output>` captures the
real BASE1 barrel and checks cold-save firing. Its ordinary tests also cover
all four player slots, pre-input acquisition, previous viewport position,
display-independent easing, target loss and the corpse gate. `test_save`
checks the optional player tail and legacy/truncated records.

```powershell
python -B tests/fixtures/generate_autoaim_reference.py .install/disc/game.cue '<US-disc.cue>' --trace .agents/tmp/functional-parity/autoaim/native.json
```
